thread:
emily: Kicking off a staged rollout for the rate-limit policy change on /v2/generate — canary at 5% for the next 30m. Policy delta: per-user/min 1200 -> 800, burst window 30s -> 20s. Will monitor 429 rate, p95 latency, token drop counts.

deploy-bot: canary deployment started for ratepolicy/v2 -> canary=5% (id: rp-2026-03-17-01) :rocket:

srinivas: Noted. Which customer cohorts are in the 5%? Is this splitting by account-id hash or by region?
emily: Splitting by account-id hash to keep partner traffic distributed. Excluding enterprise reserved tenants (they're pinned to previous policy).
lisa: Quick ask — if we see customer-facing 429s, do we rollback the canary entirely or adjust the config? I'd prefer rollback if >1% of requests across the canary are 429 in 10m window.
srinivas: Agreed on rollback threshold. Alert rule added: alert/rp-429-canary if canary_429_rate > 1% for 10m. @oncall-jun will be paged.
oncall-jun: I'll be watching. Set me up with a quick repro flow for support to validate.
jonathan: Adding a shadow rule for partners that historically have tight rate footprints (acme/*, tiny-llm/*) so we can compare responses without blocking them immediately. Shadow logs go to /logs/ratepolicy/shadow.
support-bot: heads-up — support queue #prod has a new thread: customer acme reported intermittent 429s at 12:08 UTC. Ticket 32455.
emily: Pulling metrics now — initial look: canary 429 rate at 0.35%, p95 latency +12ms, token drop negligible. Keep monitoring.
(15m later)
support-bot: Update from support: customer acme reports a spike of 429s specifically on batched requests using our sdk v1.2. They included a curl repro.
emily: Can you paste the repro request and response?
support-bot: "curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v2/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer xxxxx' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{\"model\":\"gpt-x\",\"input\":[...],\"batch_size\":8}'"
Response: HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
{ "error": "rate_limited", "retry_after": 18 }
srinivas: Interesting — batch_size 8 pushes token emission pattern; with the shorter burst window some clients that do dense batching can trip the new burst cap.
jonathan: That's exactly why we shadowed partners. Shadow shows identical traffic would have seen 429s under new policy — but enterprise pinned tenants are fine.
lisa: Decision time? With customer impact visible, I recommend aborting the canary and reverting the policy flag while we triage batching behaviour. FWIW we can also tweak burst window to 25s instead of full rollback as an intermediate, but I prefer rollback to be safe.
emily: Agreed. Rolling back canary now. Runbook step: flip canary flag to false and remove 5% routing.
(rollback command pasted by srinivas)
srinivas: Runbook cmd: 
```
# control plane API (internal)
curl -X POST "https://controlplane.internal/flags/rate_v2_canary" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $CP_SVC_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"enabled":false,"note":"rollback due to acme 429 spike 2026-03-17"}'
```

deploy-bot: canary rp-2026-03-17-01 rollback initiated by srinivas. Routing reverted to previous policy in ~45s.
oncall-jun: Confirming alerts silenced. 429 rate on canary cohort dropping back to baseline.
emily: Thanks all. Follow-ups: (1) run a focused repro with acme's SDK batch pattern in staging, (2) evaluate burst window 25s vs 30s tradeoff, (3) consider per-model burst overrides for high-throughput clients. I'll create a follow-up doc with metrics.
jonathan: I'll pull shadow logs and produce a short diff of failure traces (timestamped request/kv).
lisa: Can we notify CS to update the customer that we rolled back and will run a targeted test? @support-bot please send a calm status note to ticket 32455.
support-bot: Sending update to ticket 32455: "We rolled back a policy change after observing intermittent 429s for your traffic pattern. We're investigating and will run a targeted test with your SDK in staging; no action needed on your side for now." :white_check_mark:
emily: Closing thread for now. We'll reconvene after the staging repro (I'll ping once results are in). :raised_hands:
